guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low (active reset), flush_st is asynchronously forced to the FlushIdle state.
On the rising edge of clk_i when rst_ni is high, flush_st is updated to the value of flush_st_d.

assumptions.claim: flush_st_d continuously presents a member of the FlushState enumeration (i.e., a legal state assignment).
assumptions.cond: every clock cycle when rst_ni is high
assumptions.risk: If flush_st_d is an undefined or illegal value, flush_st may enter an invalid state, potentially disabling or corrupting the FIFO flush control logic.

uncertain_points.claim: The combinational logic generating flush_st_d is outside this chunk; cannot verify that the flush state machine correctly sequences through flush, clear, and done states under all conditions.
uncertain_points.cond: any flush request or error scenario
uncertain_points.risk: Incorrect next-state logic could leave the FIFO in an inconsistent or partially flushed state, potentially leaking or corrupting message data.

uncertain_points.claim: The reset logic only returns the flush state machine to FlushIdle; it does not directly clear the FIFO memory. The FIFO may contain key material or sensitive intermediate values that remain intact across reset.
uncertain_points.risk: If the flush logic does not perform a full FIFO wipe on reset release, sensitive cryptographic data could persist in the FIFO and be accessible after reset, violating security clear-on-reset requirements.
